vintage: Now-page data from the 2026-09-28 edition sidecar (8 changes, 2 flags); apportionment Enbridge notice Sep 16 2026; balance reconciled 2026-09-27; built 2026-09-28

changes.headline: Joliet back in service — reported
changes.dek: ~275 kb/d back online. Quantum Commodity Intelligence reported ExxonMobil said the Illinois refinery is back in service (~Sep 27, headline public, article paywalled; independent non-paywalled confirmation not found). The ~275 kb/d heavy-crude buyer returns after the Sept 13 power outage. While it was offline the Western Canadian Select (WCS) diff stayed pressured and wide; on restart the risk is a snap tighter in the front of the strip.
changes.balance_read: ~275 kb/d of WCS demand back online — the snap tighter is the front-of-strip story; the question is how much is priced.

changes.headline: De-escalation bid died over the weekend
changes.dek: Brent +~3% to ~$107 on reopen. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap Saturday — the deal that had priced Friday's -2% fade. Brent reopened +3% to ~$107, WTI ~$94. Physical flows keep healing underneath the premium: Hormuz flows back to ~13.5 mb/d (~2/3 of prewar), Saudi Gulf loadings at their strongest since the war began. But ship harassment stepped up (19 ships targeted in 48h; a tanker struck near Khasab) and the Houthis fired their heaviest salvo against Saudi Arabia since July — Yanbu, the kingdom's Hormuz-bypass hub, directly under fire.
changes.balance_read: War premium back in the price after Friday's de-escalation fade; WTI the cheaper length at a ~$11.9 spread.

changes.headline: Ukraine's biggest refining-strike weekend of 2026
changes.dek: Four plants hit in four days. Ilsky (Krasnodar, ~130 kb/d) halted Saturday; Lukoil's Perm (~252 kb/d) halted and Novoshakhtinsk knocked offline Friday (both single-source); the Moscow refinery hit in the largest one-night drone barrage of 2026 overnight Sunday. Refining capacity is being knocked out faster than it repairs, into a global distillate market at record stress — US retail diesel at an all-time high, ICE gasoil cracked ~$95/bbl vs ~$74 in August, NYH ULSD hit a record $113.48 on Sept 16.
changes.balance_read: Distillate-led tightness supports synthetic crude over Western Canadian Select (WCS) into winter; crude export impact is second-order.

changes.headline: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent de-risked
changes.dek: WTI 96th percentile; Brent -23%. Managed money in WTI sits net long +101,828 — the 96th percentile of its one-year range, the crowded lagging overhang. ICE Brent managed money net +218,114 — specs washed ~23% of their length in a single week and are already de-risked.
changes.balance_read: A de-escalation headline hits WTI length hardest; fresh escalation could drive a WTI catch-up rally off the wide Brent–WTI spread.

changes.headline: Commercial short builds on the Canadian diffs
changes.dek: -5,874 lots (WCS); -2,259 lots (SW). The in-house COT whale model flags high-confidence whale-sized commercial net-short builds on the ICE WCS 1A diff (-5,874 lots weekly) and the ICE SW 1A diff (-2,259 lots). Consistent with export-arb hedging or producer length selling the rally into Joliet's return.
changes.balance_read: Trade-house and producer hedging of the diff paper into Joliet's return — attribution hedged, not confirmed.

changes.headline: Mainline apportioned for October
changes.dek: Light 8%, heavy 4%. Enbridge's October Mainline apportionment (official notice, Sep 16): 8% on Line 2/93 lights and 4% on Line 4/67/93 heavies at Kerrobert, plus Line 1 NGL/refined FPA 7% at Regina and SPA 3% at Kerrobert. This corrects the earlier Reuters paraphrase (7% light, 10% heavy), which did not match the official notice. No force-majeure or leak headlines over the weekend on Keystone, Trans Mountain, or the Mainline. CER June data: Keystone 94% of available, Mainline ex-Gretna 94.5%.
changes.balance_read: Cross-border pipes functionally full (~272 kb/d spare on June data) heading into the fall demand window — barrels get priced, not railed.

changes.headline: EIA: bearish crude build, thin distillate
changes.dek: Crude +2.97 mb; distillate -0.43 mb. EIA weekly (w/e Sept 18): commercial crude +2.97 mb to 426.4 (bearish surprise vs a small expected draw); Cushing +2.27 to 23.7. But distillate stocks fell 0.43 mb to 107.4 — 12% below the five-year average — and refinery utilization dropped 2.8pp to 94.0% with the largest processing drop in the Midwest. That's the Joliet hole in the runs data. PADD 2 crude imports fell 595k b/d w/w to 2.437 mb/d; rising Canadian imports resume with Joliet's return.
changes.balance_read: Bearish crude headline, bullish distillate reality — the SYN-vs-WCS dislocation widens into winter.

changes.headline: Merey discounts widen on record freight
changes.dek: Offers -$14 → -$19 vs Brent. October Merey cargo offers widened from ~-$14 to ~-$19/bbl vs Brent through September — driven by freight, not fundamentals: Aframax Jose–USGC hit a $3.5M lump sum (~$7/bbl equivalent). US imports of Venezuelan crude: 583 kb/d (w/e Sept 18). Pentagon-backed NABEP has rigs and equipment lined up for Venezuela (WSJ) — plans, not barrels.
changes.balance_read: Widening Merey offers are competing length against Western Canadian Select (WCS) even when freight-driven — any USGC coker weighing Merey against WCS sees the same heavy-sour arb.

flags.title: Whiting union talks tomorrow
flags.detail: BP Whiting USW talks reconvene tomorrow (Sept 29). Settlement removes the strike wildcard; a walkout is the mirror image of Joliet — demand steps off, the WCS diff goes wider. Trigger: Strike authorization or a walkout flips this into a widening change; a settlement kills it.

flags.title: SCO supply returns ~Oct 5–mid-Oct
flags.detail: Syncrude's 50-day coker turnaround wraps ~Oct 5 and CNRL's Horizon upgrader turnaround ends ~mid-Oct — both restore synthetic-crude supply, a softener for SYN vs WCS into the fall. Trigger: Confirmed completion dates on either turnaround move this into the forward curve read.
